title: Wireless Electrochemical Measurement of Kanamycin in Whole Blood
author: Jun-Chau Chien

PalmSense software is used to perform square-wave voltammetry (SWV) continuously. The parameters are listed below. Two SWV sweeps are performed sequentially at two different frequencies. The results are subtracted to mitigate the drift. Parameters are aptamer-specific, i.e. different aptamers will need different sweeping parameters for minimum drift.

Blood circulation loop (Figure 1 and Figure 2) is created with pump and tubing to emulate actual condition. Figure 1: Schematic illustration of the blood circulation loop. The sensing probe, with the tip functionalized with aptamer sensors, is inserted into the tube through a 18G catheter. The exposed wires are connected to the potentiostat for electrochemical sensing. Figure 2: Snapshot of the blood circulation loop setup in the lab.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions for the sensing probe.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 100 micromolar stock of kanamycin aptamer (5'-HS-(CH2)6-GGGACTTGGTTTAGGTAATGAGTCCC-(CH2)7-NH-MB-3’), functionalized with a thiol at the 5' terminus and methylene blue at the 3' terminus.
Prepare a fresh TCEP solution at a concentration of 28.7 mg/mL in water.

steps.title: Fabricate and Clean Gold Wire
steps.instruction: Define the sensing area and clean the gold wire electrode.

substeps.instruction: Use heat-shrink tubing and bare gold wire (250 um) to define the sensing area at the wire tip (approximately 2 mm in length).
Perform solvent cleaning via sonication in acetone, methanol, and DI-water.
Perform electrochemical cleaning using a 3-wire electrochemical system with the following CV parameters: -0.4V to 1.5V, step = 0.001V, rate = 0.001V/sec.
Run 3 CV cycles in 200mM EC4 H2SO4.
Run 3 CV cycles in 50mM EC3 H2SO4.

steps.title: Functionalize Wire with Aptamers
steps.instruction: Immobilize the aptamers onto the gold wire surface.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 2 µL TCEP solution into an aptamer aliquot (1 µL at 100 micromolar concentration, stored at -20 °C in dry format) and incubate for 40 minutes in dark conditions.
Add 97 µL of 1X SSC buffer into the aliquot after the 40-minute incubation.
Immerse the gold wire into the TCEP-aptamer-SSC solution and incubate for 1 hour in dark conditions.
Remove the gold wire, rinse with DI-water for 1 minute, and immerse in DI-water for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Apply C6 Blocking Layer
steps.instruction: Apply the C6 solution to the functionalized wire to form a self-assembly monolayer (SAM).

substeps.instruction: Prepare C6-solution by mixing 1.245 mL of DI-water with 1 µL of C6 solution.
Immerse the gold wire into the C6-solution and incubate for 2 hours.
Rinse the gold wire with DI-water for 1 minute and immerse in DI-water for 2 minutes.
Store the gold wire in 1X SSC buffer at 4 °C overnight (24 hours) to stabilize the SAM.

steps.title: Prepare Blood Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the human whole blood samples for measurement.

substeps.instruction: Split a human whole blood sample (9 mL, stored at 4 °C) into two separate reservoirs of 4.5 mL each.
In the first reservoir, add 0.5 mL of 5mM kanamycin in SSC buffer to achieve a final concentration of 500uM.
In the second reservoir, add 0.5 mL of SSC buffer without kanamycin.

steps.title: Assemble Sensing Probe
steps.instruction: Construct the final probe to fit into an 18G catheter (approx. 6-10 cm length, 1mm diameter).

substeps.instruction: Include the functionalized gold wire as the working electrode (WE).
Include a silver chloride (AgCl) reference electrode (RE) with a diameter of approximately 100 um (prepared by immersing silver wires in bleach overnight).
Include a platinum (Pt) counter electrode (CE).

steps.title: Perform Electrochemical Measurement
steps.instruction: Insert the probe and measure the kanamycin levels in the circulating blood.

substeps.instruction: Insert the sensing probe and connect it to the electronics.
Activate the pump to circulate the blood and allow a 30-minute stabilization period.

During stabilization, perform SWV sweeps with the following parameters:
- 1st sweep: 400 Hz, 400 steps, 1mV step size, -0.4 V to 0 V, 36 mV amplitude.
- 2nd sweep: 60 Hz, 80 steps, 5mV step size, -0.4 V to 0 V, 36 mV amplitude.
After stabilization, alternate between the two samples using valves.
Store measured current in .CSV files and post-process in Matlab to extract background and signal current (difference between peak and baseline).
